claim: Computational modeling indicates that cardiac conduction may involve ephaptic coupling – intercellular communication involving electrochemical signaling across narrow extracellular clefts between cardiomyocytes.
source: Computational modeling indicates that cardiac conduction may involve ephaptic coupling – intercellular communication involving electrochemical signaling across narrow extracellular clefts between cardiomyocytes.
evidence: This claim is supported by references to computational modeling studies in the manuscript.

claim: β1(SCN1B) mediates adhesion that scaffolds trans-activating NaV1.5 (SCN5A) channels within narrow (<30 nm) perinexal clefts adjacent to gap junctions.
source: We hypothesized that β1(SCN1B) –mediated adhesion scaffolds trans-activating NaV1.5 (SCN5A) channels within narrow (<30 nm) perinexal clefts adjacent to gap junctions (GJs), facilitating ephaptic coupling.
evidence: This is the central hypothesis of the study, tested through multiple experimental approaches.

claim: Super-resolution imaging indicated preferential β1 localization at the perinexus, where it co-locates with NaV1.5.
source: Super-resolution imaging indicated preferential β1 localization at the perinexus, where it co-locates with NaV1.5.
evidence: This claim is supported by STORM imaging data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Smart patch clamp (SPC) indicated greater sodium current density (INa) at perinexi, relative to non-junctional sites.
source: Smart patch clamp (SPC) indicated greater sodium current density (INa) at perinexi, relative to non-junctional sites.
evidence: This claim is supported by electrophysiological measurements using SPC technique.

claim: βadp1 is a novel, rationally designed peptide that potently and selectively inhibited β1-mediated adhesion in electric cell-substrate impedance sensing studies.
source: A novel, rationally designed peptide, βadp1, potently and selectively inhibited β1-mediated adhesion, in electric cell-substrate impedance sensing studies.
evidence: This claim is supported by ECIS experimental data showing dose-dependent effects of βadp1.

claim: βadp1 significantly widened perinexi in guinea pig ventricles.
source: βadp1 significantly widened perinexi in guinea pig ventricles
evidence: This claim is supported by TEM measurements of intermembrane distances.

claim: βadp1 selectively reduced perinexal INa, but not whole cell INa, in myocyte monolayers.
source: βadp1 significantly widened perinexi in guinea pig ventricles, and selectively reduced perinexal INa, but not whole cell INa, in myocyte monolayers.
evidence: This claim is supported by patch clamp measurements at different cellular locations.

claim: βadp1 precipitated arrhythmogenic conduction slowing in optical mapping studies.
source: In optical mapping studies, βadp1 precipitated arrhythmogenic conduction slowing.
evidence: This claim is supported by optical mapping data showing changes in conduction velocity and arrhythmia occurrence.

claim: β1-mediated adhesion at the perinexus facilitates action potential propagation between cardiomyocytes.
source: In summary, β1-mediated adhesion at the perinexus facilitates action potential propagation between cardiomyocytes, and may represent a novel target for anti-arrhythmic therapies.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the collective experimental findings.

claim: β1-mediated adhesion may represent a novel target for anti-arrhythmic therapies.
source: In summary, β1-mediated adhesion at the perinexus facilitates action potential propagation between cardiomyocytes, and may represent a novel target for anti-arrhythmic therapies.
evidence: This is a speculative translational implication based on the study findings.

claim: The concept that the heart beats as a functional syncytium composed of discrete muscle cells electrically coupled by gap junctions is a foundational theory of modern cardiology.
source: The concept that the heart beats as a functional syncytium composed of discrete muscle cells electrically coupled by gap junctions (GJs) is a foundational theory of modern cardiology (Kléber and Rudy, 2004).
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field, supported by citation.

claim: GJ remodeling occurs in multiple cardiac pathologies.
source: Moreover, as GJ remodeling occurs in multiple cardiac pathologies (Jongsma and Wilders, 2000; Stroemlund et al., 2015), it is widely held that disrupted GJ coupling is mechanistically central to arrhythmogenesis in heart disease (De Vuyst et al., 2011; Palatinus et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Disrupted GJ coupling is mechanistically central to arrhythmogenesis in heart disease.
source: Moreover, as GJ remodeling occurs in multiple cardiac pathologies (Jongsma and Wilders, 2000; Stroemlund et al., 2015), it is widely held that disrupted GJ coupling is mechanistically central to arrhythmogenesis in heart disease (De Vuyst et al., 2011; Palatinus et al., 2012).
evidence: This represents the prevailing view in the field, supported by citations.

claim: A small group of mathematical biologists has proposed that cardiac conduction in health and disease may involve ephaptic mechanisms.
source: Whilst a GJ-based paradigm for cardiac electrical coupling has been in place for over 50 years, a small group of mathematical biologists has proposed that cardiac conduction in health and disease may involve ephaptic mechanisms (Lin and Keener, 2010; Mann and Sperelakis, 1979; Mori et al., 2008; Pertsov and Medvinskiĭ, 1979).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to theoretical/modeling studies.

claim: Ephaptic conduction is conceived as involving the intercellular transmission of action potentials via ion accumulation/depletion transients occurring within narrow extracellular clefts between closely apposed myocytes.
source: Ephaptic conduction is conceived as involving the intercellular transmission of action potentials via ion accumulation/depletion transients occurring within narrow extracellular clefts between closely apposed myocytes.
evidence: This is a definition based on theoretical work in the field.

claim: Conduction still occurs in mice with knockout of the principal ventricular GJ protein, connexin43 (Gja1/Cx43).
source: Further interest in this hypothesis has been stoked by provocative findings such as conduction still occurring in mice with knockout of the principal ventricular GJ protein, connexin43 (Gja1/Cx43) (Gutstein et al., 2001) and in humans with dominant negative mutations of GJA1, the gene encoding Cx43 (Shibayama et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to experimental findings in mice.

claim: Conduction occurs in humans with dominant negative mutations of GJA1, the gene encoding Cx43.
source: Further interest in this hypothesis has been stoked by provocative findings such as conduction still occurring in mice with knockout of the principal ventricular GJ protein, connexin43 (Gja1/Cx43) (Gutstein et al., 2001) and in humans with dominant negative mutations of GJA1, the gene encoding Cx43 (Shibayama et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to clinical observations.

claim: Theoretical studies have identified two key elements of a hypothetical structural unit that might support ephaptic conduction: 1) Close proximity (<30 nm) between the membranes of adjacent myocytes and 2) a high density of sodium channels at such points of close inter-membrane apposition.
source: Although the ephaptic hypothesis has remained controversial, owing to a lack of direct experimental evidence, theoretical studies have identified two key elements of a hypothetical structural unit that might support this alternative mechanism of conduction (Mori et al., 2008; Hichri et al., 2018; Kucera et al., 2002; Lin and Keener, 2013): 1) Close proximity (<30 nm) between the membranes of adjacent myocytes and 2) a high density of sodium channels at such points of close inter-membrane apposition.
evidence: This claim is based on computational modeling studies cited in the text.

claim: The prerequisites for the formation of a cardiac ephapse point to its likely location in the intercalated disk (ID) where cardiac sodium channels are concentrated.
source: These prerequisites for the formation of a cardiac ephapse pointed to its likely location in the intercalated disk (ID) where cardiac sodium channels are concentrated (Maier et al., 2004; Petitprez et al., 2011).
evidence: This is an inference based on theoretical requirements and known channel localization.

claim: α (Scn5a/NaV1.5) and β (Scn1b/β1) subunits of cardiac sodium channels preferentially localize at the perinexus, a nanodomain at the edge of GJs.
source: Here, we report that α (Scn5a/NaV1.5) and β (Scn1b/β1) subunits of cardiac sodium channels preferentially localize at the perinexus, a nanodomain at the edge of GJs, (Rhett et al., 2011) where the membranes of apposed cells routinely approach each other closely enough for ephapse formation (Veeraraghavan et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a key finding of the study supported by imaging data.

claim: The membranes of apposed cells at the perinexus routinely approach each other closely enough for ephapse formation.
source: Here, we report that α (Scn5a/NaV1.5) and β (Scn1b/β1) subunits of cardiac sodium channels preferentially localize at the perinexus, a nanodomain at the edge of GJs, (Rhett et al., 2011) where the membranes of apposed cells routinely approach each other closely enough for ephapse formation (Veeraraghavan et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by prior ultrastructural measurements cited.

claim: Adhesion mediated by the extracellular immunoglobulin (Ig) domain of β1 generates close proximity between the membranes of adjacent cells within perinexal nanodomains.
source: Additionally, we demonstrate that adhesion mediated by the extracellular immunoglobulin (Ig) domain of β1 generates close proximity between the membranes of adjacent cells within perinexal nanodomains, likely enabling these to function as ephapses.
evidence: This is a key finding demonstrated through multiple experimental approaches.

claim: Dynamic changes in perinexal ultrastructure, secondary to compromised β1-mediated adhesion, represent a novel mechanism for arrhythmogenic conduction defects.
source: Importantly, we identify dynamic changes in perinexal ultrastructure, secondary to compromised β1-mediated adhesion, as a novel mechanism for arrhythmogenic conduction defects.
evidence: This is a major conclusion of the study based on experimental findings.

claim: The cardiac voltage-gated sodium channel is a trimer comprised of a pore-forming alpha subunit (NaV1.5) and two non-pore-forming β subunits.
source: The cardiac voltage-gated sodium channel is a trimer comprised of a pore-forming alpha subunit (NaV1.5) and two non-pore-forming β subunits, the latter possessing an extracellular Ig domain, which facilitates adhesive interactions (Namadurai et al., 2015; O'Malley and Isom, 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge about sodium channel structure, supported by citations.

claim: The β subunits possess an extracellular Ig domain, which facilitates adhesive interactions.
source: The cardiac voltage-gated sodium channel is a trimer comprised of a pore-forming alpha subunit (NaV1.5) and two non-pore-forming β subunits, the latter possessing an extracellular Ig domain, which facilitates adhesive interactions (Namadurai et al., 2015; O'Malley and Isom, 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge about β subunit function, supported by citations.

claim: Both NaV1.5 and β1 antibodies displayed intense immunolabeling of N-cadherin (N-cad)-positive IDs in laser scanning confocal microscope (LSCM) images of guinea pig (GP) ventricular tissue.
source: Both antibodies displayed intense immunolabeling of N-cadherin (N-cad) -positive IDs (Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplement 1) in laser scanning confocal microscope (LSCM) images of guinea pig (GP) ventricular tissue and single bands at the expected molecular weights in western blots (Figure 1—figure supplement 1; detailed results from validation studies are provided in supplementary material).
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal imaging data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Both NaV1.5 and β1 antibodies displayed single bands at the expected molecular weights in western blots.
source: Both antibodies displayed intense immunolabeling of N-cadherin (N-cad) -positive IDs (Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplement 1) in laser scanning confocal microscope (LSCM) images of guinea pig (GP) ventricular tissue and single bands at the expected molecular weights in western blots (Figure 1—figure supplement 1; detailed results from validation studies are provided in supplementary material).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Both NaV1.5 and β1 antibodies displayed selective affinity for their corresponding epitopes, with no evidence of cross-reactivity to each other's epitopes in dot blot experiments.
source: Also, in dot blot experiments, both antibodies displayed selective affinity for their corresponding epitopes, with no evidence of cross-reactivity to each other's epitopes (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by dot blot data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: En face views of IDs revealed that β1 displayed a lattice-like distribution with specific immunolocalization within N-cad-free interplicate sectors of the ID.
source: While the observation of ID-enrichment of NaV1.5 (Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A) is consistent with previous studies (Maier et al., 2004; Petitprez et al., 2011), en face views of IDs reconstructed from LSCM optical sections revealed a previously unreported aspect of β1 organization (Figure 1B). In these end-on views of IDs, β1 displayed a lattice-like distribution with specific immunolocalization within N-cad-free interplicate sectors of the ID (Figure 1B, Figure 1—figure supplement 3C).
evidence: This is a novel finding supported by confocal imaging data in Figure 1B.

claim: Interplicate regions of the ID are well-characterized as being enriched in Cx43 GJs.
source: Interplicate regions of the ID are well-characterized as being enriched in Cx43 GJs (Severs, 2000).
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field, supported by citation.

claim: Punctate Cx43 immunosignal corresponding to GJ demonstrated close association with the strands comprising the β1 lattice.
source: In line with this, punctate Cx43 immunosignal corresponding to GJ demonstrated close association with the strands comprising the β1 lattice (Figure 1—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal imaging data.

claim: A significant proportion of immunolocalized NaV1.5 molecules were organized into clusters preferentially localized adjacent to clusters of Cx43 molecules (i.e. GJs).
source: A significant proportion of immunolocalized NaV1.5 molecules were organized into clusters preferentially localized adjacent to clusters of Cx43 molecules (i.e. GJs; Figure 1C), while a population of NaV1.5 molecules was also observed co-distributing with N-cad (Figure 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by STORM imaging data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: A population of NaV1.5 molecules was observed co-distributing with N-cad.
source: A significant proportion of immunolocalized NaV1.5 molecules were organized into clusters preferentially localized adjacent to clusters of Cx43 molecules (i.e. GJs; Figure 1C), while a population of NaV1.5 molecules was also observed co-distributing with N-cad (Figure 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by STORM imaging data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: β1 molecules organized into a lattice-like distribution with β1 strands punctuated by tight side-by-side association with Cx43 clusters.
source: In contrast to NaV1.5, β1 molecules organized into a lattice-like distribution with β1 strands punctuated by tight side-by-side association with Cx43 clusters (Figure 1E), but extending almost exclusively through N-cad-free interplicate zones of the ID (Figure 1F).
evidence: This claim is supported by STORM imaging data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: β1 strands extend almost exclusively through N-cad-free interplicate zones of the ID.
source: In contrast to NaV1.5, β1 molecules organized into a lattice-like distribution with β1 strands punctuated by tight side-by-side association with Cx43 clusters (Figure 1E), but extending almost exclusively through N-cad-free interplicate zones of the ID (Figure 1F).
evidence: This claim is supported by STORM imaging data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Nearly half of ID-localized NaV1.5 clusters (48.1%) were located adjacent to Cx43 GJ, constituting a perinexal pool.
source: In accordance with visual assessment (Figure 1), STORM-RLA indicated that nearly half of ID-localized NaV1.5 clusters (48.1%) were located adjacent Cx43 GJ (Figure 2A,C), a sub-population we term the perinexal pool.
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative STORM-RLA analysis shown in Figure 2.

claim: The perinexal pool of NaV1.5 included 31% of NaV1.5 clusters that did not overlap Cx43 clusters, and an additional 17.1% which tangentially overlapped Cx43 clusters.
source: This pool included 31% of NaV1.5 clusters that did not overlap Cx43 clusters, and an additional 17.1% which tangentially overlapped Cx43 clusters (Figure 2A,B,C).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative STORM-RLA analysis shown in Figure 2.

claim: A second, plicate pool of NaV1.5, localized to N-cad-rich plicate ID regions, was found to contain 29% of ID-localized NaV1.5.
source: A second, plicate pool of NaV1.5, localized to N-cad-rich plicate ID regions, was found to contain 29% of ID-localized NaV1.5 (Figure 2A,B,D), consistent with previous reports from us (Veeraraghavan and Gourdie, 2016) and the Delmar group (Leo-Macias et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative STORM-RLA analysis and is consistent with prior studies.

claim: Nearly half (48.3%) of ID-localized β1 clusters were identified within perinexal nanodomains.
source: Closely paralleling the NaV1.5 case, nearly half (48.3%) of ID-localized β1 clusters were also identified within perinexal nanodomains (Figure 2A,E).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative STORM-RLA analysis shown in Figure 2.

claim: Only 7.6% of β1 clusters were co-located with N-cad clusters, suggesting that 92.4% of ID-localized β1 clusters are located in N-cad-free, GJ-rich interplicate ID regions.
source: However, only 7.6% β1 clusters were co-located with N-cad clusters (Figure 2A,F), suggesting that an overwhelming 92.4% of ID-localized β1 clusters are located in N-cad-free, GJ-rich interplicate ID regions.
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative STORM-RLA analysis shown in Figure 2.

claim: The pore-forming subunit NaV1.5 is divided between two significant pools within the ID, a perinexal pool, and a plicate pool.
source: In summary, the pore-forming subunit NaV1.5 is divided between two significant pools within the ID, a perinexal pool, and a plicate pool; however, the β1 subunit is mainly localized in perinexal, and other interplicate ID sites.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on STORM-RLA data.

claim: The β1 subunit is mainly localized in perinexal, and other interplicate ID sites.
source: In summary, the pore-forming subunit NaV1.5 is divided between two significant pools within the ID, a perinexal pool, and a plicate pool; however, the β1 subunit is mainly localized in perinexal, and other interplicate ID sites.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on STORM-RLA data.

claim: The extracellular Ig domain of β1 facilitates adhesive interactions, including trans homophillic interaction with β1 molecules on neighboring cells.
source: The extracellular Ig domain of β1 facilitates adhesive interactions, including trans homophillic interaction with β1 molecules on neighboring cells (Calhoun and Isom, 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge about β1 function, supported by citation.

claim: Junctional resistance was markedly higher (>3 fold) in 1610 β1OX cells, compared to cells without β1 (1610 Parental).
source: Junctional resistance was markedly higher (>3 fold) in 1610 β1OX cells, compared to cells without β1 (1610 Parental; Figure 3A), consistent with the expression of β1 increasing levels of adhesion between the cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by ECIS measurements shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The expression of β1 increases levels of adhesion between cells.
source: Junctional resistance was markedly higher (>3 fold) in 1610 β1OX cells, compared to cells without β1 (1610 Parental; Figure 3A), consistent with the expression of β1 increasing levels of adhesion between the cells.
evidence: This is an inference from the ECIS data showing increased junctional resistance.

claim: Immunosignals for tight junction proteins and Ca2+-dependent cadherins were below detectable levels, and did not change with β1 expression in 1610 cells.
source: Immunosignals for tight junction proteins and Ca2+-dependent cadherins were below detectable levels, and did not change with β1 expression (data not shown), suggesting that these proteins were unlikely to account for adhesion observed between 1610 cells.
evidence: This claim is based on immunolabeling experiments, though data not shown.

claim: The strategy for preparing a rationally designed antagonist of β1-mediated adhesion was based on an approach successfully applied to two other adhesion proteins of the Ig domain family that share homologies with β1: N-cad and desmoglein-1.
source: Our strategy for preparing a rationally designed antagonist of β1-mediated adhesion was based on an approach successfully applied to two other adhesion proteins of the Ig domain family that share homologies with β1: N-cad (Williams et al., 2000a; Williams et al., 2000b) and desmoglein-1 (Schlipp et al., 2014).
evidence: This describes the methodological approach, supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The method involves synthesizing a peptide mimicking the adhesion sequence within the Ig loop domain.
source: This method involves synthesizing a peptide mimicking the adhesion sequence within the Ig loop domain.
evidence: This describes the methodological approach based on prior work.

claim: The location of the adhesion receptor in sodium channel β Ig domain has been characterized in previous structure and function studies.
source: The location of the adhesion receptor in sodium channel β Ig domain has been characterized in previous structure and function studies (Brackenbury and Isom, 2011; Malhotra et al., 2000; Patino et al., 2009).
evidence: This is established knowledge from prior studies, supported by citations.

claim: A molecular homology model of β1 was generated using SWISS-MODEL based on the recently resolved crystal structure of β3, and structural data from cryo-electron microscopy studies of β1 in the electric eel.
source: Based on the recently resolved crystal structure of β3, and structural data from cryo-electron microscopy studies of β1 in the electric eel, we generated a molecular homology model of β1 using SWISS-MODEL (Figure 3B) (Namadurai et al., 2014).
evidence: This describes the computational modeling approach used, with citation.

claim: An amino acid sequence (1FVKILRYENEVLQLEEDERF20: βadp1) within the β1 Ig domain is homologous to the desmoglein-1 Ig loop adhesion sequence.
source: We then identified an amino acid sequence (1FVKILRYENEVLQLEEDERF20: βadp1) within the β1 Ig domain homologous to the desmoglein-1 Ig loop adhesion sequence - a peptide mimetic of which acts as a competitive inhibitor of desmosomal adhesion (Harrison et al., 2016).
evidence: This describes the identification of the peptide sequence based on homology.

claim: βadp1 associated with the adhesion surface of the Ig loop when allowed to bind freely to the β1 homology model in silico.
source: To assess the interaction of βadp1 with β1, and thus its potential ability to act as a competitive inhibitor of β1 adhesion, we allowed the peptide to bind freely to the β1 homology model in silico, determining that it associated with the adhesion surface of the Ig loop (Figure 3C).
evidence: This claim is supported by computational docking studies shown in Figure 3C.

claim: MM-GBSA refined docking of βadp1 using Maestro displayed a low energy conformation (ΔG binding −44.47) at the adhesion surface location.
source: MM-GBSA refined docking of βadp1 using Maestro displayed a low energy conformation (ΔG binding −44.47) at this location.
evidence: This claim is supported by computational docking calculations.

claim: The predicted binding pose revealed stabilization via a network of intramolecular hydrogen bonds, and electrostatic interactions between the C-terminal end of βadp1 and polar residues within the β1 adhesion domain.
source: The predicted binding pose revealed stabilization of this conformation via a network of intramolecular hydrogen bonds, and electrostatic interactions between the C-terminal end of βadp1 and polar residues within the β1 adhesion domain, as well as accommodation of hydrophobic residues of βadp1 within pockets along the β1 adhesion surface.
evidence: This describes the molecular interactions predicted by computational modeling.

claim: Sequences of similar length from the Ig loop outside of the adhesion domain, as well as a randomized βadp1 sequence (βadp1-scr), did not show propensity to interact with the adhesion surface of the β1 extracellular domain.
source: Sequences of similar length from the Ig loop outside of the adhesion domain, as well as a randomized βadp1 sequence (βadp1-scr), did not show propensity to interact with the adhesion surface of the β1 extracellular domain.
evidence: This claim is supported by computational docking studies with control sequences.

claim: Substituting the basic arginine (R) at position 19 of βadp1 with acidic aspartic acid (D) yielded a sequence (βadp1-R85D) with significantly abrogated binding to the β1 model in silico (ΔG binding −18.05).
source: Substituting the basic arginine (R) at position 19 of βadp1 with acidic aspartic acid (D) yielded a sequence (βadp1-R85D) with significantly abrogated binding to the β1 model in silico (ΔG binding −18.05).
evidence: This claim is supported by computational docking studies with the mutant peptide.

claim: The arginine at position 19 of βadp1 corresponds to R85 on full length β1 and is a mutational hotspot associated with diseases of electrical excitation in the heart and brain of humans.
source: The arginine at this position of βadp1 corresponds to R85 on full length β1 and is a mutational hotspot associated with diseases of electrical excitation in the heart and brain of humans (Calhoun and Isom, 2014; Thomas et al., 2007).
evidence: This is established knowledge from clinical genetics, supported by citations.

claim: βadp1 significantly, persistently and dose-dependently decreased junctional resistance in confluent monolayers of 1610 β1OX cells, but not in 1610 parental cells.
source: We next assessed the ability of βadp1 to abrogate β1 adhesion using the 1610 β1OX model. βadp1 significantly, persistently and dose-dependently decreased junctional resistance in confluent monolayers of 1610 β1OX cells, but not in 1610 parental cells (Figure 3D), which express negligible levels of β1.
evidence: This claim is supported by ECIS measurements shown in Figure 3D.

claim: βadp1 selectively inhibited the intercellular adhesion function of β1 in the 1610 β1OX model.
source: These results suggest that βadp1 selectively inhibited the intercellular adhesion function of β1 in this in vitro model.
evidence: This is an inference from the ECIS data showing selective effects on β1-expressing cells.

claim: βadp1 efficiently and dose-dependently inhibited the formation of intercellular interactions between sub-confluent 1610 β1OX cells forming into monolayers.
source: Similarly, βadp1 efficiently and dose-dependently inhibited the formation of intercellular interactions between sub-confluent 1610 β1OX cells forming into monolayers (Figure 3E), doing so at lower concentrations of peptide than necessary for established confluent monolayers of β1 over-expressing cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by ECIS measurements shown in Figure 3E.

claim: βadp1 inhibited the formation of intercellular interactions at lower concentrations of peptide than necessary for established confluent monolayers of β1 over-expressing cells.
source: Similarly, βadp1 efficiently and dose-dependently inhibited the formation of intercellular interactions between sub-confluent 1610 β1OX cells forming into monolayers (Figure 3E), doing so at lower concentrations of peptide than necessary for established confluent monolayers of β1 over-expressing cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by comparison of ECIS data from different experimental conditions.

claim: Neither the treatment of 1610 β1OX cells with βadp1-R85D, nor the treatment of 1610 parental cells with βadp1 affected the establishment of cell-cell contacts, as assessed by ECIS.
source: Neither the treatment of 1610 β1OX cells with βadp1-R85D (Figure 3—figure supplement 1), nor the treatment 1610 parental cells with βadp1 (Figure 3D,E) affected the establishment of cell-cell contacts, as assessed by ECIS.
evidence: This claim is supported by ECIS measurements with control peptides and control cells.

claim: βadp1 showed no evidence of toxic effects on 1610 β1OX cells, or the mouse ventricular myocyte cell line H9C2 even at concentrations twice that used elsewhere in this study.
source: βadp1 showed no evidence of toxic effects on 1610 β1OX cells, or the mouse ventricular myocyte cell line H9C2 even at concentrations twice that used elsewhere in this study (Figure 3—figure supplement 2), suggesting that the peptide's action was unlikely to result from cellular toxicity.
evidence: This claim is supported by cell viability assay data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: The peptide's action was unlikely to result from cellular toxicity.
source: βadp1 showed no evidence of toxic effects on 1610 β1OX cells, or the mouse ventricular myocyte cell line H9C2 even at concentrations twice that used elsewhere in this study (Figure 3—figure supplement 2), suggesting that the peptide's action was unlikely to result from cellular toxicity.
evidence: This is an inference from the cell viability data.

claim: Perinexal ID regions show high enrichment for β1.
source: LSCM and STORM results described above demonstrate that perinexal ID regions show high enrichment for β1.
evidence: This is a summary of imaging findings from earlier in the manuscript.

claim: Perfusion of βadp1 into Langendorff-perfused GP hearts had profound yet highly selective effects on the ultrastructure of perinexal regions.
source: Perfusion of βadp1 into Langendorff-perfused GP hearts had profound yet highly selective effects on the ultrastructure of these regions (Figure 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by TEM data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Biotinylated βadp1 (βadp1-b; 100 µM) localizes in perinexal regions of the ID adjacent to Cx43 immunosignal.
source: A confocal image of a section from a GP ventricle perfused with biotinylated βadp1 (βadp1-b; 100 µM) in Figure 4A shows punctate βadp1-b signal (red) adjacent to Cx43 immunosignal (green), consistent with the peptide localizing in perinexal regions of the ID.
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal imaging data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: βadp1 treatment induced a de-adhesion of the β1-enriched membranes of the perinexus.
source: Representative images (Figure 4B) obtained by transmission electron microscopy (TEM) illustrate close apposition between perinexal membranes in control tyrode-perfused GP ventricles and markedly wider spacing between perinexal membranes in βadp1-treated hearts, reflecting that βadp1 treatment induced a de-adhesion of the β1-enriched membranes of the perinexus.
evidence: This claim is supported by TEM data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Quantification of TEM images indicated that βadp1 increased inter-membrane distance in dose-dependent fashion within perinexi, but not at other ID locations distal from GJs.
source: Overall, quantification of TEM images indicated that βadp1 increased inter-membrane distance in dose-dependent fashion within perinexi, but importantly, not at other ID locations distal from GJs (Figure 4C).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative TEM analysis shown in Figure 4C.

claim: A scrambled control peptide (βadp1-scr; 10 µM) did not significantly affect inter-membrane spacing at perinexal or non-perinexal ID sites.
source: In contrast, a scrambled control peptide (βadp1-scr; 10 µM) did not significantly affect inter-membrane spacing at perinexal or non-perinexal ID sites.
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative TEM analysis with control peptide.

claim: βadp1 selectively, and dose-dependently, widened β1-enriched perinexi, consistent with the specific antagonism of β1-mediated adhesion within the ID by the inhibitory peptide.
source: These results indicate that βadp1 selectively, and dose-dependently, widened β1-enriched perinexi – a dehiscence of these nanodomains that would be consistent with the specific antagonism of β1-mediated adhesion within the ID by the inhibitory peptide.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the TEM data.

claim: β1-null ventricles displayed striking evidence of perinexal de-adhesion, with > 4 fold greater perinexal inter-membrane distances compared to wild-type (WT) littermates.
source: To further investigate the effects of loss of β1 function on perinexal ultrastructure, we examined ventricles from Scn1b -/- (β1-null) mice. β1-null ventricles displayed striking evidence of perinexal de-adhesion, with > 4 fold greater perinexal inter-membrane distances compared to wild-type (WT) littermates, while inter-membrane distance at non-perinexal ID sites was not different between the two genotypes (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by TEM data from β1-null mice shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Neither βadp1, nor a scrambled control peptide (βadp1-scr), measurably altered the sodium current (INa) in isolated, non-contacting myocytes.
source: As a first step to assess the effects of βadp1 on intercellular conduction of electrical impulse, we undertook voltage and current clamp studies on single myocytes isolated from GP hearts to determine whether the peptide affected AP and/or sodium channel function properties independent of whether cells where attached to one another. Neither βadp1, nor a scrambled control peptide (βadp1-scr), measurably altered the sodium current (INa; Figure 5A–D) or the duration or morphology of action potentials (APs; Figure 5E–F), suggesting that neither peptide affected the function of the Na+ channel complex, or other ion channels, in isolated, non-contacting cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by patch clamp data from isolated myocytes shown in Figure 5.

evidence: This claim is supported by confocal imaging data from NRVMs shown in Figure 6A.

source: Under control conditions, local INa density at junctional sites proximal to Cx43-EGFP fluorescence, quantified by SPC, was significantly greater than that measured at non-junctional sites (Figure 6—figure supplement 2B), in line with previous reports of higher INa density at the ID relative to the lateral membrane (Lin et al., 2011).

claim: Neither peptide altered whole cell INa density in NRVMs.

claim: βadp1 impaired conduction in Langendorff-perfused GP hearts.

source: In keeping with the observed QRS prolongation, βadp1 treatment dose-dependently slowed transverse conduction in intact ventricles, increasing the anisotropy of conduction, and precipitating spontaneous arrhythmias. We have previously demonstrated in silico that anisotropic conduction slowing secondary to a reduction of INa at the ID results from compromised ephaptic coupling (Veeraraghavan et al., 2015): Briefly, a wavefront traveling transverse to the fiber axis encounters more cell-cell junctions per unit distance than one traveling longitudinally.
